title: useQuery
subtitle: Main React hook for reactive data fetching
description: The primary hook for reactive data fetching with automatic re-renders on state changes. Perfect for server state management with built-in caching, background updates, and error handling.

rows.name: queryKey
rows.description: Unique identifier for the query. Can be a string, array, or object.

rows.name: options
rows.description: Optional configuration object. If no fetcher is provided, uses a previously registered fetcher.

rows.name: options.fetcher
rows.description: Function that returns a Promise resolving to the data. Optional if fetcher was already registered.

rows.name: options.staleTime
rows.description: Time in milliseconds after which data is considered stale.

rows.name: options.refetchOnSubscribe
rows.description: When to refetch data when component subscribes.

returns.description: Object containing the current query state

properties.name: data
properties.description: The fetched data, undefined while loading or on error

properties.name: isLoading
properties.description: True if the query is currently fetching for the first time

properties.name: isFetching
properties.description: True if the query is currently fetching (including background refetches)

properties.name: error
properties.description: Error object if the query failed, null otherwise

properties.name: isError
properties.description: True if the query failed with an error

properties.name: isSuccess
properties.description: True if the query succeeded and has data

behavior.title: Automatic Re-renders
behavior.description: Component automatically re-renders when query state changes

behavior.title: Background Updates
behavior.description: Stale data is refetched in the background without blocking UI

behavior.title: Error Handling
behavior.description: Built-in error states with retry capabilities

behavior.title: Caching
behavior.description: Automatic caching with configurable stale time

dos: Use descriptive query keys that include all dependencies
Handle loading and error states appropriately
Set appropriate staleTime for your data freshness requirements
Use TypeScript for better type safety
donts: Don't mutate the returned data object directly
Don't forget to handle error states in your UI
Don't use useQuery for one-time operations (use fetchQuery instead)
Don't create new objects in the fetcher function on every render

callouts.title: Performance Tip
callouts.content: useQuery automatically deduplicates identical requests and shares cache between components.

callouts.title: Memory Management
callouts.content: Query cache is automatically cleaned up when no components are using a query.
